'''[[Hampshire County Council elections|Elections]] to [[Hampshire County Council]]''' took place on 6 May 2021 as part of the [[2021 United Kingdom local elections]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Election Timetable in England|url=https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/920186/Election_Timetable_in_England_2019.pdf|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200924235544/https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/920186/Election_Timetable_in_England_2019.pdf |archive-date=2020-09-24 |access-date=|website=}}</ref> All 78 seats were up for election, with each ward returning either one or two councillors by first-past-the-post voting for a four-year term of office. This took place at the same time as the elections for the [[Hampshire Police and Crime Commissioner]] and district councils.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Elections and voting|url=https://www.hants.gov.uk/en/aboutthecouncil/electionsandvoting|access-date=2021-01-04|website=www.hants.gov.uk|language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Background ==
Whilst an election for the county council had already been planned, [[districts of England|district council elections]] were delayed due to the ongoing [[COVID-19 pandemic]], meaning that they are due to be held at the same time as the Hampshire County Council Elections.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2020-03-13|title=Coronavirus: English local elections postponed for a year|language=en-GB|work=BBC News|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-politics-51876269|access-date=2021-01-05}}</ref> Whilst not part of Hampshire County Council, the [[Unitary authorities of England|unitary authorities]] of [[2021 Portsmouth City Council election|Portsmouth]] and [[2021 Southampton City Council election|Southampton]] are also due to hold council elections for a third of their respective councils at the same time.

After the previous election in 2017, the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservatives]] held 56 seats, the [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]] 19, [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] 2, and [[Community Campaign (Hart)|Community Campaign Hart]] 1.

In July 2019, Cllr Floss Mitchell resigned from the Conservative Party to sit as an unaffiliated [[Independent politician|independent]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Floss Mitchell|url=https://www.facebook.com/FlossMitchellCllr/posts/2368770960111478|access-date=2021-01-05|via=Facebook|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-01-05|title=Councillor details - Councillor Floss Mitchell|url=https://democracy.hants.gov.uk/mgUserInfo.aspx?UID=186|access-date=2021-01-05|website=democracy.hants.gov.uk|language=en-GB}}</ref>

In December 2019, Cllr Michael Westbrook left the Labour Party alongside borough councillors to form the Basingstoke & Deane Independent Group<ref>{{Cite web|title=Nine former Labour councillors team up with independents to form new political party|url=https://www.basingstokegazette.co.uk/news/18100023.nine-former-labour-councillors-team-independents-form-new-political-party/|access-date=2021-01-05|website=Basingstoke Gazette|language=en}}</ref> sitting with Community Campaign Hart as an independent grouping on the County Council.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-01-05|title=Councillor details - Councillor Michael Westbrook|url=https://democracy.hants.gov.uk/mgUserInfo.aspx?UID=1382|access-date=2021-01-05|website=democracy.hants.gov.uk|language=en-GB}}</ref>

In December 2020, Conservative Cllr Keith Evans died from COVID-19.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-12-29|title=Tributes paid to Hampshire county councillor who died from Covid-19|url=https://www.itv.com/news/meridian/2020-12-29/tributes-paid-to-hampshire-county-councillor-who-died-from-covid-19|access-date=2021-02-28|website=ITV News|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Councils pay tribute after death of 'dedicated' county and borough councillor|url=https://www.dailyecho.co.uk/news/18975088.tributes-paid-hampshire-county-councillor-keith-evans/|access-date=2021-02-28|website=Daily Echo|language=en}}</ref>

As such, the Conservatives and Labour lost two councillors and a single councillor respectively, in the time since the previous election.

The [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservatives]] won 56 seats, the same number as in the previous election. [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] won 3 seats, an increase of 1. [[Community Campaign (Hart)|Community Campaign Hart]], which had previously held 1 county council seat, failed to secure the two seats they ran in. An [[Independent politician|Independent]] candidate won in [[2021 Hampshire County Council election#Eastleigh (8 seats)|Bishopstoke & Fair Oak]], and the Whitehill & Bordon Community Party won [[2021 Hampshire County Council election#East Hampshire (7 seats)|the seat they ran in of the same name]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-05-06|title=Election results by division, 6 May 2021|url=https://democracy.hants.gov.uk/mgElectionElectionAreaResults.aspx?EID=27&RPID=15979367|access-date=2021-05-09|website=democracy.hants.gov.uk|language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Results by electoral division==
Hampshire County Council is divided into 11 districts, which are split further into electoral divisions, and then split into a number of wards. 
Councillors seeking re-election were elected in [[2017 Hampshire County Council election|2017]], and are compared to that year's polls on that basis.
